content.text: You’re a digital creator in Nigeria. Stripe isn’t available. PayPal suspends accounts without warning. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are inaccessible. This isn’t a temporary problem. It’s a structural exclusion baked into the payment [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-kyc-payment-gateways-digital-sellers-2|COREMERCH guide to infrastructure]] of the internet. The solution isn’t another workaround. It’s a permanent shift to sovereign commerce infrastructure — [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-google-apps-script-digital-commerce-21|architecture]] you own, control, and deploy. This breakdown explains how.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Online gumroad

Sovereign commerce infrastructure is a complete digital commerce stack designed to operate independently of platforms like Stripe, PayPal, or Gumroad. It’s built on open, permissionless tools that no single company or country can restrict. For creators in regions where payment processors are unavailable or unreliable, this architecture removes the middleman entirely. Instead of renting access to someone else’s platform, you deploy your own. The stack handles hosting, payment verification, order storage, and product delivery without relying on any third-party service that could lock you out. This isn’t a hack — it’s base-layer infrastructure. Once deployed, you own it. No subscriptions. No platform fees. No geographic restrictions.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The stack combines free, globally accessible tools into a unified system. Hosting is handled by GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages — both free and CDN-backed for fast global delivery. Backend logic runs on Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, which execute code without servers. Orders are stored in Supabase (a free, open-source alternative to Firebase) or Google Sheets. Product files are delivered via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Payments are processed through NOWPayments, which verifies on-chain crypto transactions with a 0.5% fee and no KYC. The system is stateless: no customer data is stored, and no platform has access to your operations. Everything is automated. A buyer sends payment. The blockchain confirms it. The product is delivered instantly. No platform required.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This infrastructure is built for digital creators in countries where Stripe operates in only 46 out of 195 nations, where PayPal can suspend accounts for 180 days without appeal, and where platforms like Gumroad are inaccessible. It’s for sellers in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Tanzania, the Philippines, and beyond. These creators sell ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, beats, plugins, software, and other digital products. They need a system that doesn’t depend on a platform’s approval or a country’s inclusion on a whitelist. Sovereign commerce infrastructure gives them that. It’s not a temporary fix — it’s a permanent alternative built to withstand financial isolation and platform rejection.
Stripe operates in only 46 out of 195 countries. Sovereign infrastructure works in all 195.
The Components That Make It Work Together

Each component in the stack is chosen for its accessibility, reliability, and independence. GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages provide static hosting with global CDNs, ensuring fast load times everywhere. Cloudflare Workers and Google Apps Script handle backend logic without requiring servers, reducing costs and complexity. Supabase and Google Sheets store order data securely and scalably. Google Drive and Cloudflare R2 deliver product files directly to buyers. NOWPayments integrates seamlessly, verifying crypto payments on-chain and triggering instant product delivery. The stack is modular: you can swap components as needed. For example, if Google Sheets becomes unavailable, switch to Supabase. If BSC network fees rise, accept Solana or TRON payments instead. The architecture is designed to adapt, not break.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

Deployment starts with choosing the right stack for your needs. The Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) uses GitHub Pages, Google Apps Script, and NOWPayments — ideal for launching quickly with up to 3 products. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) upgrades to Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and includes SPF/DKIM/DMARC email configuration for professional delivery. Both stacks are deployed in 48 hours, fully tested, and handed off with 30-day support. If you prefer to build yourself, The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) provides complete documentation, source code, and scaling guidance. The Complete Builder Kit ($197) includes all blueprints and templates for instant download. Every option gives you full ownership of your infrastructure. No platform can shut you down. No country can lock you out. Visit https://coremerch.github.io/products.html to deploy your stack today.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

If Stripe, PayPal, or Gumroad aren’t available in your country, deploy sovereign commerce infrastructure. This combines free, globally accessible tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments to handle hosting, payment verification, order storage, and product delivery. The system is automated, stateless, and doesn’t rely on any platform or payment processor. Once deployed, you own the entire stack. No subscriptions. No geographic restrictions. It’s built to work anywhere, for anyone, permanently.
PayPal can suspend your account for 180 days with no appeal. Own your stack — no platform can hold your funds.

If you’re searching for Stripe alternatives in Nigeria or Gumroad replacements in restricted countries, sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a structural solution. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) deploys Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments in 48 hours, configured for professional use. For a full list of deployment options, visit https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. This isn’t a workaround — it’s a permanent shift to infrastructure you own.
Your Deployment Checklist

Choose your stack based on your product volume and technical needs. For the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or Edge Commerce Stack ($197), purchase through https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. Provide your product details and payment preferences. COREMERCH deploys your stack in 48 hours, fully tested and ready to sell. If building yourself, download The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) or Complete Builder Kit ($197) for step-by-step documentation and source code. Configure NOWPayments to accept your preferred cryptocurrencies. Test the entire flow end-to-end. Launch your store. Own your infrastructure.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this if I’m not a developer?

Yes. The Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) and Edge Commerce Stack ($197) are deployed for you, fully configured and tested. No coding required. If building yourself, The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) provides plain-language documentation and templates.
What cryptocurrencies should I accept for low fees?
BSC, Solana, and TRON networks have transaction fees under $0.10. Configure NOWPayments to accept these for cost-effective payments. Avoid Ethereum for small transactions due to high gas fees.
Can platforms like PayPal or Stripe shut this down?

No. This infrastructure doesn’t rely on PayPal, Stripe, or any third-party platform. Payments are verified on-chain via NOWPayments, and product delivery is handled directly through your stack. No platform has access or control.
What happens if a component like Google Sheets becomes unavailable?
The stack is modular. If one component fails, swap it for an alternative. For example, replace Google Sheets with Supabase for order storage. The architecture is designed to adapt, not break.
Do I need to store customer data?
No. The system is stateless. Payments are verified on-chain, and products are delivered directly. No customer data is stored, ensuring compliance with privacy regulations and reducing liability.
